context:
Owner decision 2026-11-19 (choice dialog): rule (1) for both revert:, and Revert " forms. A revert that deletes the reverted change's changelog.d fragment was unreleased and needs nothing (the deletion satisfies the check); otherwise the change shipped and the revert needs a fragment. Revert " loses its blanket exemption.

Implemented intent of the owner rule: identify reverted commits from 'This reverts commit <sha>'; unidentifiable means a fragment is required; the revert's paths must be a subset of the reverted commit's paths; a reverted commit's own unreleased fragment must be deleted (no new fragment), a released one needs a new fragment, and an internal revert needs none; deleting any other fragment never satisfies the check.

2026-11-20 done: #4397 merged (9703d6d9). One rule for revert: and Revert " titles: reverted commits come from 'This reverts commit <sha>'; unidentifiable means a fragment is required; the PR's paths must be a subset of the reverted commit's, and its net diff must byte-for-byte invert the cited commit (git patch-id --verbatim over raw-bytes git diff --binary; empty diff or missing id = unverified); the reverted change's unreleased fragment must be deleted (a dangling symlink is not a deletion) and then no new fragment is needed; a released fragment needs a new one; an internal revert needs none; deleting any other fragment never satisfies. pr-open and CI decide identically; trunk-revert output passes. description:
scripts/changelog_fragments.py exempts GitHub-style `Revert "..."` titles but not the conventional-commit `revert:` type, which is in neither EXEMPT_TYPES nor REQUIRED_TYPES; when a changed path ships in the package it falls through to "unrecognised title type 'revert'" and requires a fragment, and both make pr-open and the CI changelog check (ci.yml, run from a trusted base copy) refuse. Because --added-files-from counts only added files, deleting the reverted change's fragment never satisfies the check. While landing #4200 (revert of #4196), pr-open refused the `revert:` title; the PR landed as `Revert "..."`. Conversely, `Revert "` skips the fragment even when it reverts a change that already shipped. scripts/trunk_revert.py generates `Revert "` titles.

Decision gate (owner), one rule for both forms: (1) if the diff deletes a changelog.d fragment, the reverted change was unreleased, so no fragment is needed and the deletion satisfies the check; otherwise the reverted change shipped and needs a fragment. Under (1) the owner also decides whether `Revert "` stays blanket-exempt. Or (2) always exempt `revert:` as `Revert "` is today.

Guardrails: keep breaking-title (!) handling; no change to required types feat, fix and perf; pr-open and CI must give the same decision.
